edges.description: Organisms from the urinary or abdominal focus enter the bloodstream.
Circulating organisms lodge in the vertebral endplate and disc.
Circulating E. coli is detected as positive blood cultures.
Seeded organisms proliferate within the disc-endplate niche.
Gram-negative cell-wall lipopolysaccharide activates TLR4-dependent inflammatory responses in disc and bone-marrow cells.
Infection spreads contiguously out of the discovertebral unit.
Local disc and vertebral infection produces focal spinal pain.
The infected focus, with or without ongoing bacteremia, causes a systemic febrile response.
The infected focus drives an acute-phase response.
An established vertebral focus can keep seeding the blood, producing persistent bacteremia.
Osteoclastic resorption and inflammatory disc-cell injury erode the endplates and the disc.
Disc destruction collapses the intervertebral space.
Endplate erosion contributes to mechanical and inflammatory spinal pain.
Contiguous spread forms paravertebral or psoas abscesses.
Spread into the vertebral canal forms an epidural abscess.
Epidural collections compress the cord or nerve roots.
Compression of the cord or lumbar roots weakens the legs.
Cervical cord compression weakens all four limbs.
Breaching the mucosa of a colonized urinary tract releases E. coli into the bloodstream.
